content:
Maya Chen: heads-up — onboarding Surfacer-28B (int4) to canary. seeing intermittent OOMs on p2 nodes during long generations. repro at ~max_new_tokens 1024 for some prompts.
Sam R: thanks — is this on dedicated canary or hosted?
Maya Chen: hosted canary. only ~5% of requests fail but they blow out memory and fragment GPU. tail latency spikes.
Liam O'Connor: any patterns on batch size / concurrency?
Maya Chen: yes. failures cluster when batch_size >= 4 and max_new_tokens > 512. small batches fine.
Nora Patel: reminds me of past slot fragmentation with large KV caches. did we enable prefetch/WARMUP for this model?
Maya Chen: prefetch=on by default for new int4 models. I tried disabling prefetch locally and saw fewer OOMs on a smoke run.
Sam R: can you paste the runtime config you used?
Maya Chen: here — minimal patch I rolled locally: ```
model: surfacer-28b-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  preferred_batch_size: [1,2,4]
  batch_timeout_ms: 6
prefetch:
  enabled: false
kv_cache:
  max_slots_reserved: 0.55
  slot_compactor: enabled
generation:
  max_new_tokens_default: 256
  max_seq_len: 4096
```
Liam O'Connor: interesting — lowering default max_new_tokens to 256 is a good stopgap. but that changes QoE for long-form tasks.
Nora Patel: we should add an adaptive limit: default 256 but allow explicit override via route config; plus an autoshrink for concurrent long requests.
Maya Chen: agreed. Infra note: when prefetch was on, GPU memory map showed many small free blocks (fragmentation). disabling prefetch led to larger contiguous free areas.
infra-bot: deploy status: canary cluster surfacer-28b-int4 v0.3.1 -> rolled to 4/6 pods
Sam R: can we try a hybrid: prefetch only for short generations and disabled for long max_new_tokens? implies we need a heuristic by requested max_new_tokens.
Liam O'Connor: implementable in router: if max_new_tokens >= 512, route to prefetch=false pool. we already have policy-based routing.
Maya Chen: quick perf numbers from local bench (synthetic long prompt): with prefetch ON + batch 4 -> OOM after ~120s. prefetch OFF + batch 4 -> completes, 2.1s median token time, GPU mem usage steadier.
Nora Patel: any quantization quality regressions from int4? eval-bot, did eval suite show drift?
eval-bot: surfacer-28b-int4 on eval-suite-v2: Rouge-L delta to float32: -0.8%; answer correctness micro-F1: -1.2% on KBQA. within acceptable thresholds for canary.
Sam R: OK quality looks fine. Priority is reliability. propose immediate Canary patch: 1) set default max_new_tokens to 256, 2) prefetch heuristic by requested max_new_tokens, 3) reduce max_batch_size to 2 for canary pool, 4) enable slot_compactor sweep every 10m.
Maya Chen: I pushed patch branch `canary/surfacer-mem-safety` with the changes. running canary smoke now.
infra-bot: smoke-run: 50 long-gen requests -> 0 OOMs, 3 timeouts (retries), 47 success. old canary had 6 OOMs for same test.
Liam O'Connor: good signal. we should add a runtime metric: fragmentation_ratio = largest_free_block / total_free_mem. track per-model.
Sam R: +1. add an alert if fragmentation_ratio < 0.35 for >5m.
Nora Patel: also add an internal eval that runs a small number of long generations at low QPS to exercise compactor and eviction. scheduled as nightly canary health check.
Maya Chen: rolling patch to all canary pods. will hold on prod until we run 12h canary.
Sam R: action items: Maya — monitor fragmentation_ratio & tail OOMs for 12h and paste logs. Liam — add router rule for prefetch=false when max_new_tokens>=512. Nora — add nightly long-gen smoke eval. I'll own post-canary rollback plan.
Maya Chen: logs (snippet): ```
[2026-03-20T22:14:02Z] alloc failed: requested=1.2GiB free_chunks=127 small_frag=0.42 largest_free=512MiB total_free=1.6GiB
[2026-03-20T22:14:02Z] OOM during kv_allocate slot=14 seq=1024
[2026-03-20T22:14:03Z] compactor_trigger: start slot=14 -> migrated 8 entries
```
Liam O'Connor: that's classic fragmentation. compactor migration looks expensive but worth it infrequently. maybe increase sweep frequency during low QPS windows.
Nora Patel: we should also try a lightweight kernel tweak: enable per-request temp_scratch allocator that returns memory back more eagerly. takes some risk. do as feature flag.
Sam R: agreed feature flag first. Maya deploys with flag:false for canary, enable if we still see issues.
Maya Chen: will update the PR with flag gating and a dashboard. tagging @oncall for visibility.
infra-bot: alert created: frag_ratio_low surfacer-28b-int4-canary -> notify eng-ml #pager 30min window
Maya Chen: thanks team — will post canary metrics in this thread when 12h completes. :thumbsup:
Liam O'Connor: great. if 12h looks stable we can plan a staged rollout to reserved dedicated clusters with slightly more conservative defaults.
Nora Patel: note to self: add a notebook to reproduce fragmentation locally (script + prompt set). will attach later.
Maya Chen: attaching quick checklist in PR description for rollout steps and rollback criteria.
Sam R: perfect. closing for now, reopen if canary misbehaves.
